exposure: cervical dilatation at non-labour caesarean section
Cervical dilatation at non-labour caesarean section
cohort: 199 pregnant women undergoing non-labour caesarean section
finding: Intra-operative cervical dilatation at non-labour caesarean section does not significantly reduce post-operative pain or impact maternal morbidity but is associated with thinner endometrial cavity thickness, shorter operation time, and shorter hospitalisation duration.
mod_finding: Intra-operative cervical dilatation during cesarean section does not seem to benefit postoperative pain, change in haemoglobin concentrations, or puerperal fever.
